subject: Retainer vs. Credit Sculpting — finalizing protection model

Subject: Retainer vs. Credit Sculpting — initial options

Hi Olivia / procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to put two concrete protection models in writing so you can share with finance and procurement: a Retainer model (prepaid monthly retainer that guarantees Xms response lanes and a set number of priority credits) and a Credit Sculpt model (consumption-based credits with dynamic drawdown and per-incident caps).

High-level differences:
- Retainer: predictable monthly fee, includes guaranteed 1-hour P1 response window, 3x on-call escalations/week, and 10% of monthly tokens as priority credits. Rollforward allowed up to 2 months.
- Credit Sculpt: lower base cost, credits consumed when incidents breach token/latency thresholds, credits can be applied as post-facto offsets. No guaranteed on-call retainer but 4-hour P1 window and optional pay-as-you-go fastpath.

Attachments: SLA_Pricing_Options_v2.pdf (matrix + examples) — see attached for sample pricing across commit levels.

Quick asks:
1) Which model would procurement prefer to evaluate first?
2) Are there specific PO/contract requirements we should be aware of (billing cadence, invoicing entity)?

If helpful, Ben and I can run a short pricing walkthrough this afternoon.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Ava — thanks for this. Procurement is reviewing; a few clarifying questions before we escalate to finance: 

1) Uptime tiers — your doc shows 99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99. Can you confirm how each maps to credit consumption and whether credits are tiered per-incident or aggregated monthly?
2) Rollforward — you mentioned 2 months for the retainer. Is that negotiable for enterprise pilots (we'd prefer 3 months if possible).
3) Response windows — we need guaranteed contact within 30 minutes for P0 incidents during business hours. Is that part of the retainer or an add-on?
4) Auditability — procurement will require an incident log export and token-level consumption report monthly. Do you provide an automated export?

Also, who is the billing contact? We need the AP-side name for the paperwork.

Thanks — please reply over email so we have written answers for our legal team.

Best,
Olivia Porter
Head of Product Operations, NeptuneAI
olivia.porter@neptuneai.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2025 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Retainer vs. Credit Sculpt — procurement questions (draft answers)

Ava / Laura — forwarding Olivia's procurement questions. Drafting suggested responses below that we can send back as a single email. Feel free to edit.

Suggested answers: 
- Uptime tiers: Credits are aggregated monthly; each uptime band maps to a slab consumption rate (example: 99.9 -> 5 credits per 0.1% below SLO aggregated monthly; 99.95 -> 3 credits per 0.01%; 99.99 -> 1 credit per 0.001%). We should include an example table (I'll attach in the final).
- Rollforward: We can extend retainer rollforward to 3 months for initial 6-month pilots; after pilot will revert to 2 months standard.
- Response windows: 30-minute contact for P0 is included in the Retainer Plus add-on (adds 20% to the retainer). Standard retainer includes 1-hour P1. We should present both price points.
- Auditability: Yes — we provide monthly token-level consumption CSV and incident export via the Console. We can push a scheduled export to a Neptune S3 bucket if required (SLA addendum required).

Next steps I propose: 1) Ava to respond with updated matrix and explicit examples, 2) Attach new SLA addendum (docx) showing S3 export option and rollforward term, 3) Offer a short call with procurement Monday to sign off.

I'll build the slab example and attach.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Product Pricing
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Retainer vs. Credit Sculpt — procurement questions (answers + updated proposal)

Hi Olivia / team — thanks for the clear questions. Attached are the updated artifacts: SLA_Pricing_Options_v3.pdf (includes the slab examples and two price points for Retainer vs Retainer Plus), and Redwood_Terms_SLA_Addendum.docx (audit/export language and rollforward clause). Short answers below for your legal/procurement record.

- Uptime tiers and credit accounting:
  • Credits are aggregated monthly. We calculate monthly SLO attainment and apply the slab at the monthly level (not per-incident). See p.4 of the attached PDF for the math and an example month.
  • Example: If the agreed SLO is 99.95 and observed availability is 99.85 over the month, the delta maps to the 99.95 slab (0.10% below) and consumes 10 credits under the standard slab in the matrix.

- Rollforward:
  • For pilots up to 6 months we can offer a 3-month rollforward on unused retainer credits. After concluding the pilot, standard term is 2 months. This will be called out in the addendum.

- Response windows:
  • P0 30-minute contact is handled by Retainer Plus (20% uplift). Standard Retainer includes 1-hour P1 and 4-hour P0 contact. The difference is availability of the fastpath on-call roster.

- Auditability / exports:
  • We provide an automated monthly CSV export (token-level) and incident export. We can deliver to a Neptune-managed S3 bucket via our secure transfer flow; the addendum includes required encryption and retention details.

Billing contact for Redwood invoices:
  • Laura Bennett, Finance Operations — laura_bennett@redwood.ai. We bill monthly in arrears unless you prefer net-30 prepaid for the retainer.

Next steps: 
1) If procurement is comfortable with the above, we'll issue a final quote and a DocuSign-ready SLA addendum. Link to HubSpot (HS-374829) and draft DocuSign included.
2) If you prefer the Credit Sculpt model, we can provide the consumption projection for the last 3 months to show likely credit drawdowns.

I can make myself available tomorrow at 11am PT for a 30-minute call to finalize.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
